verdict.rationale: Decagon lets users define natural-language criteria that are applied automatically. Watchtower reviews every interaction against custom criteria and flags what matches, and AOPs define agent behavior in natural language. Proactive agents reach out "at the right moments," which implies event-driven triggers. However, nothing documents a general event→rule→action engine: the only automatic action evidenced is flagging, and no trigger configuration is described. Missing for 10: documented event-trigger configuration (e.g. on ticket created, status change, external system event), a range of automatic actions beyond flagging/surfacing, explicit rule-definition docs for proactive outreach triggers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Define what matters using natural language. From "mentions of frustration" to "violations of data privacy policy," Watchtower understands your flagging criteria and applies your intent contextually.
Watchtower reviews every interaction against your custom criteria and surfaces what matters most.
you can define agent behavior in natural language, the same way you train human agents with SOPs
